feature_name: Checkout Pricing and Coupons (Cart to Order)

critical: FIXED DURING THIS RUN — `button-name` (1 node, /cart): the button that removes an applied coupon was an icon-only <button> with no accessible name, so a screen-reader user could apply a coupon but had no way to know how to remove it. It appeared on every step where a coupon was applied (alt-08, alt-09). Fixed by frontend-developer (aria-label="Remove coupon <CODE>", icon marked aria-hidden) and re-captured: the re-run of the cart-edits spec reports zero critical violations and `color-contrast` as the only remaining rule.
serious: `color-contrast` — 88 node-instances summed across the run, on 9 routes (/account, /account/orders/[id], /cart, /checkout, /checkout/confirmation/[id], /products/business-cards, the two PDPs). This is the same site-wide token-level contrast finding the Product Catalog and Quantity Pricing runs reported, not something this feature introduced: it is attributable to the routes, not to the coupon/pricing controls, and it is present on pages that contain none of this feature's UI. It still blocks a clean WCAG AA pass and is worth fixing once at the theme-token level rather than per screen.
moderate: `heading-order` (1 node each on /checkout/confirmation/[id] and /account/orders/[id]) — a heading level is skipped on the two order-summary screens, so the money breakdown is not reachable as a properly nested section by heading navigation. Low effort, and these are exactly the screens a customer is most likely to re-read.

`landmark-main-is-top-level`, `landmark-no-duplicate-main`, `landmark-unique` (1 node each, on /account and /account/orders/[id]) — the account area renders a nested/duplicated <main>, so landmark navigation lands in the wrong place. Pre-existing on the account shell, not introduced by checkout.
accessibility_summary.coverage_caveat: automated scan only — manual/screen-reader review still needed

performance_summary.initial_load: VOID — `url_mismatch: true`. Lighthouse requested /account but audited http://localhost:3000/auth/login?redirect=%2Faccount. The storefront keeps its access token in memory only (features/auth/store.ts partialize) and the session is restored from an httpOnly refresh cookie that capture.js's `seedDefaultContextStorage` cannot copy, so an audit of any authenticated route is redirected to the login page. The reported 0.28 performance / 0.95 accessibility / 0.73 best-practices are the LOGIN page's numbers and must not be read as the account page's. This is the same structural failure mode pipeline/README.md documents for the admin panel; it is now confirmed to apply to the storefront too, for authenticated routes only.
performance_summary.final_state: VOID for the same reason — requested /account/orders/20936, audited /auth/login?redirect=%2Faccount%2Forders%2F20936. `warm_cache: true` would make it non-comparable to a cold load even if the URL had matched.
concerns: Both checkpoints are unusable as written; future checkout runs should either set `lighthouse: 'off'` (as the other three specs in this feature already do) or checkpoint on a public route such as a PDP, which needs no session.
These would be Next.js dev-server numbers in any case, not a production build — useful only as a run-over-run baseline, never as a shippable score.
No performance signal was collected for the two screens that matter commercially (the review step and the confirmation page), so nothing in this run says whether the checkout is fast enough.

ux_gaps.issue: An applied coupon is never re-validated when the cart changes. err-12 proves it: a coupon with a ₹3,000 minimum is applied to a ₹4,450.00 cart, the customer removes a line, and the cart still advertises '−₹445.00' (10% of the OLD subtotal) on a ₹2,200.00 cart. `features/cart/store.ts`'s own comment claims the coupon is 'cleared when items change significantly', but no code does that. The customer only discovers it at the review step, which then shows 'Could not confirm pricing: Minimum order amount for this coupon is ₹3000.00' alongside the reassuring 'shown amounts are estimates. You can still place the order' — and placing it is guaranteed to fail. Deciding what should happen (silently drop the coupon, re-validate on every cart mutation, or block checkout) is a product call, not a mechanical fix.
ux_gaps.related_edge_case: Coupon validated at the cart, then the cart changes so the coupon no longer qualifies

ux_gaps.issue: Coupon product/category restrictions are stored, exposed and editable but never enforced. `coupons.applicable_product_ids` / `applicable_category_ids` are written by POST /admin/coupons and echoed by AdminCouponResponse, but neither `coupon_service.validate_for_customer` nor `order_service._compute_order` reads them. Verified end to end: QA-CHECKOUT-PRODONLY, restricted to product 17 (T-shirts), discounted a cart containing none of that product by the full ₹445.00 at both /coupons/validate and /orders/preview. Any product-scoped promotion run today silently discounts the whole catalogue. The fix needs a semantic decision first (scope the discount basis to the matching lines, or refuse the coupon outright), so it is flagged rather than dispatched.
ux_gaps.related_edge_case: Coupon restricted to specific products or categories (applicable_product_ids)

ux_gaps.issue: A cart line removed within ~500 ms of a full page load comes back. `CartSyncProvider` debounces its sync by 500 ms, and its login-merge path unions local and server lines (`mergeCartItems` re-adds anything server-only), so a removal that has not yet been pushed is undone by the next hard navigation. Observed directly on the first run of the error spec: /cart read ₹2,200.00 with 2 lines and the review step then read ₹4,450.00 with 3 products. A deleted line and a line added on another device are indistinguishable to that merge. Narrow window, but the direction of the failure is wrong — it resurrects something the customer deleted, on the screen immediately before payment.

The review step's failure copy is too soft when the preview itself failed. 'Could not confirm pricing — shown amounts are estimates. You can still place the order.' is right for a network blip but wrong for a 422 the server will raise again on create (an invalid coupon, an out-of-range quantity); in that case the Place Order button is a guaranteed dead end that still shows a total built from client estimates.
ux_gaps.related_edge_case: Coupon validated at the cart, then the cart changes so the coupon no longer qualifies

ux_gaps.issue: The email sign-in form reports every failure as 'Invalid email or password. Please try again.', including a 429 from the 10/hour rate limit on POST /auth/login — so a customer who is merely rate-limited is told their credentials are wrong and will keep retrying. Found while building this run's sign-in helper, not by a capture step.

Coverage gap, not a defect: the 'rush' turnaround could not be exercised. Both products that define it (Matte Finish Business Cards +₹300, Custom Die-Cut Stickers +₹500) have `is_active: false` on that option in the dev data, so the PDP correctly does not render it and the server correctly answers 422 `invalid_turnaround` for it. Standard (+₹0) and Express (+₹150 / +₹200) were both charged and verified; the rush surcharge path has no live data to test against.
ux_gaps.related_edge_case: Rush turnaround advertised in print_specs but inactive

ux_gaps.issue: Console noise, not a defect: three steps (hp-07, hp-08, alt-04) record `404 (Not Found)`. Reproduced deterministically — it is `next/image` proxying `https://cdn.urgentprinters.com/product/2a979355823148079c1bbfd08b5ded14_lg.webp`, a dev-catalogue image that does not exist on the CDN. Unrelated to checkout. The other two console errors are the API doing its job and are expected: 422 at err-12 (coupon minimum not met) and 409 at edge-03 (price_changed).

recommendations.action: Decide and implement what a product/category-restricted coupon should mean, then enforce it in `coupon_service` and `order_service` (both paths — validate and create). Until then, treat `applicable_product_ids`/`applicable_category_ids` in the admin UI as a trap: it looks like a working control and discounts everything. This is the only finding in this run that can cost real margin.

Re-validate (or clear) an applied coupon whenever the cart's contents change, so the cart can never advertise a discount the server will refuse. Pair it with a narrower review-step message: when the preview failed with a 4xx the server will repeat, say so and disable Place Order instead of offering 'you can still place the order'.

Make the cart's server sync removal-safe: either flush the pending sync on page unload, or give the merge enough information (a tombstone / per-line updated_at) to tell a deleted line from a line added on another device. Today a removal inside the 500 ms debounce window is silently undone by the next page load.

Fix the two moderate landmark/heading findings on the order-summary screens (/checkout/confirmation/[id], /account/orders/[id]) — one skipped heading level and a duplicated <main> in the account shell. Small, and they are on the screens customers return to.

Stop collecting Lighthouse on authenticated storefront routes until the audit can carry the session: both checkpoints in this run measured the login page. Either set `lighthouse: 'off'` for checkout specs or checkpoint on a PDP.

Address `color-contrast` once at the theme-token level rather than per screen — 88 node-instances across 9 routes, present on pages with none of this feature's UI, and unchanged since the previous two pipeline runs.

Distinguish a 429 from bad credentials in the email sign-in form, and give the dev catalogue a product image that resolves (or a local placeholder) so the PDP stops logging 404s that mask real errors.
